title: Proof contract meta-schema
description: The shape a proof contract must satisfy. A proof contract declares no JSON Schema dialect of its own because it is discharged by a bespoke checker in verification support rather than by a schema validator, so nothing validated its own shape. The checkers deserialize into typed structs: a missing required key fails loudly, but a key the struct defaults fails silently, and a misspelled optional key silently empties the constraint it names while the attestation stays green. Every branch below closes to additional properties so a misspelled key is rejected rather than ignored. This meta-schema guards the project's own method and is not published under a versioned URI.

oneOf.title: Reference boundary contract
oneOf.description: Constrains one module's source to reference, or never reference, named symbols.

searchPaths.description: Roots scanned for the forbidden references, each a repository-relative path. Present instead of module where the contract guards a tree rather than one file, because a per-module contract only reaches the modules somebody remembered to write one for.

oneOf.title: Argument vector policy contract
oneOf.description: Constrains the structure of a generated argument vector.

oneOf.title: Construction boundary contract
oneOf.description: Constrains construction of one named type to a named set of modules, over a whole search tree rather than one module. The reference boundary branch above names the module it guards, so guarding a tree that way means remembering to add a contract for each module added to it, and the module nobody remembered is exactly the one that bypasses the invariant. This branch inverts that: the search paths are scanned whole, and any construction outside the permitted set is a counterexample, so a new module is guarded the day it is written by a contract nobody edited.

constructedType.description: The type whose construction is bounded, named as the source names it. The checker matches a construction expression rather than the bare token, so the type's own declaration is not a counterexample and neither is a mention in a comment or an import.

permittedModules.description: The modules allowed to construct the type, each a repository-relative source path. An empty list would forbid construction everywhere, including where the value has to come from, so the list carries at least one entry.

searchPaths.description: The roots scanned for construction, each a repository-relative path. Named here rather than taken from the project's tooling configuration so the contract states its own scope: a checker that silently scanned nothing would report a clean bill, and the floor the checker asserts is that these paths were read and were not empty.

oneOf.title: Latency budget contract
oneOf.description: Declares the wall-clock ceiling each named seam must be observed to meet. The ceilings exist in production as constants either way; declaring them here makes them one list a scenario can attest rather than four numbers nobody measured.

oneOf.title: Deserialization strictness contract
oneOf.description: Requires a derive attribute on every deserializable struct under the named paths, so a document key the model does not define is refused rather than silently dropped. Unit-variant enums are strict by construction, since an unrecognised value is already an unknown-variant error, so the requirement binds struct types and struct-variant enums.

searchPaths.description: Repository-relative paths whose deserializable types the requirement binds.

exemptTypes.description: Types the requirement does not bind, each a deliberate decision rather than an oversight.

oneOf.title: Duplication allowance contract
oneOf.description: Declares the size at or above which the duplication scanner is consulted. The scanner fingerprints shape with identifiers normalised, so below that size it cannot tell a copied body from the shape small functions share and is not asked; at or above it, structural identity is copied logic and the gate is zero with no exemption available. allowedConstants answers the constant census, which exists because the scanner carries no unit kind for a constant and so cannot see one at any threshold.

allowedConstants.description: The duplicated constants a constant census reports that are coincidence rather than copies, each with the reason it is one. Carries no minimum, because none excused is the healthy resting state and the census scenario's own floor guards the reader rather than this list. A constant is keyed by name and declaration together, so an entry names the constant rather than a content fingerprint.

minimumLines.description: Source lines a unit must carry before the scanner is consulted about it. Bounded above because the threshold is the whole gate: raised far enough, the scanner reads almost nothing and reports no group, which is indistinguishable from a clean tree. The ceiling is set by the subject rather than by a coverage figure, since a copied body of a dozen lines is duplication anyone would act on.
